title: Lock contention: an injected workload spins on a futex at high rate

problem.summary: An injected workload spins on a futex at high rate. The deciding evidence is a container that was absent before the window and present during it, identified by its event RATE and its softirq share rather than by its futex share. SCOPE OF THIS SIGNATURE. This fault is injected as a separate sidecar container, so what is described here is the footprint of an injected workload, not of lock contention arising inside a service. A real application holding a lock too long would show the futex pressure in the SERVICE container and no newcomer would appear at all. Treat a match as evidence that an injected workload of this shape is present, and say so rather than claiming the application itself is contended.
symptoms: a service is slow but its CPU is not saturated
latency is erratic rather than uniformly higher
the slowdown does not follow a call path to a dependency

discriminators.signal: the newcomer container's kernel event rate and softirq share
discriminators.this_problem: 62,774-63,380 events/s and 4.8-5.9% softirq across 6 runs on two applications
discriminators.not_this_problem: DO NOT decide this by finding the container with the highest futex share. Measured on two applications: the injected container sits at 41-47% futex against siblings at 33% on one, and at 52-58% against siblings at 60% on the other. Where services run on a JVM, threads park on futexes and an ordinary service is futex-heavy by nature, so the comparison inverts and the rule names an innocent service. Use the newcomer test and the rate.
discriminators.evidence: MEASURED 28-09-2026 on 6 runs across two applications, by locating the injected container from its process names rather than assuming it is the busiest or the most futex-heavy.

unverified_do_not_claim.claim: raised runqueue delay identifies lock contention
unverified_do_not_claim.status: NOT TESTED HERE - and known to fire everywhere
unverified_do_not_claim.measurement: the cpu-contention-co-tenant blueprint already measured runqueue delay as raised in every CPU-family fault and in healthy load bursts. It was demoted to corroboration there and is not reinstated here.
unverified_do_not_claim.consequence: not used. Decide on the futex share.

reproduction.teardown: the recipe restores state; verify against /sys/fs/cgroup
harness_only: the fault is injected as a sidecar container, which is a property of our harness. In production the same mechanism occurs inside an existing service - so the SHAPE transfers, the newcomer shortcut does not

collection_order.why_these: MEASURED BASIS. Every discriminator in this blueprint is a share of these event groups within one container. Nothing else in the trace is required, and no other modality is used - this blueprint was built and validated on kernel traces alone.

processing.expect: a CTF directory with metadata and channel streams

processing.step: Find containers that are active during the window and absent before it
processing.expect: one container with substantial traffic during the window and none before. If none appears, this blueprint does not apply - say so and stop

processing.step: Measure what share of its own events that container spends on each kind of work
processing.expect: the share profile below, within the measured range

processing.step: Apply the rules and emit the verdict
processing.expect: a verdict naming the container and the mechanism, or an explicit abstain
one page showing the shares, the cut, and what was ruled out

outputs.contains: culprit container pid_ns, its event shares, and the shares of every other container for comparison
per-container event shares for the window
each family's measured share on the deciding axis, with this run's value marked

verdict_when: a container is present in the window that was absent before it
it produces {NEWCOMER_BUSY_PER_S} kernel events per second or more
its softirq share is BELOW {SOFTIRQ_INVERSION_MIN}, which is what separates it from priority inversion

rule_out.when: softirq is {SOFTIRQ_INVERSION_MIN} or above - measured 10.9-13.4% there against 4.8-5.9% here
the newcomer produces {NEWCOMER_IDLE_PER_S} events per second or fewer - it is parked, not spinning
the newcomer's futex share is near zero - a stress workload, not a lock

decision.root_cause_is: the newcomer container, named by its pid_ns

provenance.authored_by: measured from StrataTrace v2 kernel traces
provenance.notes: Rewritten 28-09-2026. The generated version decided on 'the container whose futex share is far above every other container', which was measured to invert between the two applications - 41-47% against siblings at 33% on one, 52-58% against siblings at 60% on the other. Replaced with a newcomer test plus event rate and softirq share, both of which held to within a few percent across both applications. The over-fitting caveat is stated in the summary: this is a sidecar injection, so the signature is partly our injector's.

apply_when: a service is slow without being CPU-saturated
latency is erratic rather than uniformly raised
a kernel trace is available and futex syscalls are traced
do_not_apply_when: no container is new to the window
an EXISTING container went silent - that is a stopped dependency
the suspect is an ordinary service with a high futex share and no arrival - on a JVM that is normal, not a fault
applicability.cheap_precheck: find a container present in the window and absent before it, then read its events per second: at or above {NEWCOMER_BUSY_PER_S} is one of the spinning faults, at or below {NEWCOMER_IDLE_PER_S} is a deadlock.

stopping_conditions.conclude: a newcomer matched the rate and softirq ranges above
stopping_conditions.stop_and_switch: a discriminating share falls outside its measured range
stopping_conditions.stop_insufficient: no container is new to the window. Say so rather than naming the most futex-heavy container, which on a JVM application is an ordinary service

applicable_symptoms: a service is slow but its CPU is not saturated
latency is erratic rather than uniformly higher
the slowdown does not follow a call path to a dependency

historical_effectiveness.note: shares measured on 5 runs of this family

evidence_sufficiency.if_below_floor: report the shares and say which blueprint they sit between
evidence_sufficiency.report_when_stuck: the container's shares and every sibling's, side by side
